b2-03-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Writing the New Words
b2-03-01.scenario: In 1912, in the New York Coffeehouse in Pest, Frigyes Karinthy asks you, a young writer at the next table, why your new book took you so long. You tell him that making up the new words took a lot of time.
b2-03-01.prompt: Tell Karinthy what took a lot of time when you wrote your book.
cues: Say that it was about the new words
Say what you did to them: create them (use the noun)
Say that it took a lot of time
b2-03-01.target: Az új szavak megalkotása sok időt vett igénybe.
b2-03-01.english: The creation of the new words took a lot of time.
b2-03-01.canDo: I can derive action and result nouns from verbs using -ás/-és.

b2-03-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Took the Week
b2-03-02.scenario: At the New York Coffeehouse, Karinthy asks you what you were doing all week for your essay. You tell him about rephrasing the text and imitating the sentences.
b2-03-02.prompt: Tell Karinthy what took your time this week.
cues: Name the text and what you did to it (rephrase)
Name the sentences and what you did to them (imitate)
Say that both took a lot of time
b2-03-02.target: A szöveg átfogalmazása és a mondatok utánzása sok időt vett igénybe.
b2-03-02.english: The rephrasing of the text and the imitation of the sentences took a lot of time.
b2-03-02.canDo: I can convert 'Verb + Direct Object' phrases into possessive nominalizations ('a szöveg átfogalmazása').

b2-03-03.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Parody
b2-03-03.scenario: In the coffeehouse, Karinthy asks when you understood what his parody of a poet was really about. You tell him that it was after you had read it.
b2-03-03.prompt: Tell Karinthy when you understood the criticism.
cues: Say that you understood the criticism after that
b2-03-03.target: A paródia elolvasása után megértettem a kritikát.
b2-03-03.english: After reading the parody, I understood the criticism.
b2-03-03.canDo: I can combine possessive nominalizations with postpositions ('után', 'előtt', 'során', 'révén', 'helyett').

b2-03-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Say It Simply
b2-03-04.scenario: Karinthy reads you a stuffy sentence from an essay: 'A hibák kimutatása után elmentek.' He asks you to say the same thing as a plain clause with a verb.
b2-03-04.prompt: Say Karinthy's sentence again as a clause with a finite verb: after they pointed out the mistakes, they left.
cues: Begin with the word for 'after' as a conjunction
Say what they did to the mistakes (pointed them out)
b2-03-04.english: After they pointed out the mistakes, they left.
b2-03-04.canDo: I can unpack a noun chain with 'után' or 'során' into a clause with a finite verb.

b2-03-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Secret of the Book
b2-03-05.scenario: A reader in the New York Coffeehouse asks you, a fellow writer, why Karinthy's book was such a success. You tell the reader what the secret of its success was.
b2-03-05.prompt: Tell the reader the secret of the success of Karinthy's book.
cues: Name whose success it was and say 'the secret of its success'
Say that the criticism was never malicious
b2-03-05.target: A könyv sikerének a titka az volt, hogy a kritika soha nem vált rosszindulatúvá.
b2-03-05.english: The secret of the book's success was that the criticism never became malicious.
b2-03-05.canDo: I can read a short text about Karinthy's 'Így írtok ti' and answer questions about it.

b2-03-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Karinthy's Book
b2-03-consolidation.scenario: Karinthy meets you again in the coffeehouse and asks how the work on the essay went and what you think of his book. You answer in two short sentences.
b2-03-consolidation.prompt: Tell Karinthy how the work on the text went and what the secret of his book is.
cues: Say that rephrasing the text was hard work
Say what the secret of the book's success is: accurate observation
b2-03-consolidation.target: A szöveg átfogalmazása nehéz feladat volt. A könyv sikerének a titka a pontos megfigyelés.
b2-03-consolidation.english: Rephrasing the text was a hard task. The secret of the book's success is accurate observation.
b2-03-consolidation.canDo: I can recognize and construct single and double possessive nominalization chains (-ás/-és).
